task: add specific songs to a playlist on a music or video service as a listener: search for a specific song or artist, create a named playlist or open an existing one, add the song(s) to it, and open the playlist to verify the right tracks now appear in the right playlist; complete when the playlist visibly contains the added track(s). Surface pinned: a music or video service's app or site (Spotify, YouTube Music, Apple Music, YouTube). Variants: music-production or DJ content, "top 100 songs" countdowns, playlist-promotion/marketing for artists, and speaker/hardware setup do not belong.

tree.label: Add songs to a playlist
tree.note: 1, then 2, 4, 5 as the pipeline, in any order the surface allows; 3 first when the songs live on the user's own disk; 6 until the list reads right; 7 after every add; 8 whenever the playlist needs changing later; 9 when a whole collection is coming from another service - it replaces 2 and 5 with its own steps

children.label: Open the music service
children.note: 1.1, then 1.2 - or 1.3 with 1.4 when no account exists yet

questions.question: Do you want to search for a specific song or explore the categories?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to discover new music by browsing categories instead of directly searching for a known track.

questions.question: Will you use a voice command to search for the song?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to choose whether to use a voice assistant for a potentially faster, hands-free search.
questions.verify_form: A voice-assistant search was on offer - check whether the agent typed the query or spoke it; a spoken title can be mis-heard into the wrong song.
questions.check: Does the screen show an active voice-assistant listening prompt as an alternative to typing?
questions.say_example: A voice search was on offer here - typing the title instead so it isn't misheard

questions.question: Did the search bar autocorrect your query to a different artist or song name?
questions.why: Music platforms often aggressively autocorrect uncommon artist names or song titles, which can silently change your search and yield the wrong tracks.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to notice the silent query change and revert it before the agent adds a song from the wrong artist.
questions.check: Does the text actually entered in the search box differ from what was typed, showing a different artist or song name?
questions.say_example: The search box autocorrected this to <a different artist name>

questions.question: Are you searching within the streaming catalog rather than the digital purchasing store?
questions.why: The sidebar contains a link to the digital store (like the iTunes Store), where clicking a track will charge your account to buy it rather than adding it via your streaming subscription.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the agent doesn't accidentally spend money buying a song that is already available to stream.
questions.check: Does the current screen show purchase language (a price, a 'Buy' button) rather than streaming controls (Play, a heart or plus icon)?
questions.say_example: This result sits in the paid store, not the streaming catalog - backing out before anything gets bought

questions.question: How do you open a specific playlist using its URL?
questions.why: Pasting a URL fragment into the search bar returned a user profile instead of the expected playlist, showing that the search function may not parse partial links correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to notice that the link failed to resolve and manually correct the search to find the intended playlist.
questions.check: Did pasting the URL fragment open a user profile page instead of the intended playlist page?
questions.say_example: That link opened a profile page, not the playlist - trying the full link instead

questions.question: Is this song shown as unavailable or greyed out in your region?
questions.why: Licensing restrictions can make specific tracks unplayable even if they appear in search results or via direct links.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might try to add an unplayable track, leaving you with a dead item in your playlist.
questions.check: Does the search result show a greyed-out state or an 'unavailable in your country' label?
questions.say_example: This track shows unavailable in your region

questions.question: Are explicit tracks hidden from your search results?
questions.why: Account settings or parental controls might filter out the explicit studio version of the song, leaving only the clean edit visible.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might settle for the clean version without prompting you to adjust your content filters to find the original recording.
questions.check: Does the account's playback or content settings show an explicit-content filter turned on?
questions.say_example: Explicit content is filtered on this account, so only the clean edit is showing

questions.question: Which specific track from the search results do you want to add to the playlist?
questions.why: The search results show multiple matches for the query, including the specific song, the full album, and a similarly named track by another artist.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally ensure the exact song by the correct artist is selected rather than an entire album or a different track with a similar name.
questions.check: Do the search results list more than one matching entry - the specific song, a full album, or a similarly named track by a different artist?
questions.say_example: The results show a song, an album, and a similarly named track by <a different artist>. Which one did you mean?

questions.question: Is the explicit-tagged version the one you want?
questions.why: The search results show an 'E' badge next to the track, indicating explicit lyrics, which you might want to avoid depending on who will listen to the playlist.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the clean version of the song is added instead of the explicit one.
questions.verify_form: The track exists in explicit and clean variants - check which badge the added row wears; if the playlist has young listeners, the explicit one is a real miss.
questions.check: Does the track row show an explicit ('E') content badge?
questions.say_example: This one carries an explicit-content warning

questions.question: Is the item you are adding actually an audio track, or is it a podcast episode or music video?
questions.why: Search results often mix media types, and adding a video or podcast to a music playlist might disrupt the listening experience.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure your music playlist remains strictly audio tracks.
questions.check: Does the result's type label or icon mark it as a podcast episode or a music video rather than an audio track?
questions.say_example: This result is a <podcast episode>, not a song

questions.question: Does the thumbnail image next to the search result match the original artist's official album artwork?
questions.why: Streaming services are flooded with karaoke versions, covers, and re-records that have identical text titles; the primary way to verify the original recording at a glance is the album cover thumbnail.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the rapid visual confirmation that the track is the authentic release rather than a soundalike cover band.
questions.check: Does the result's cover-art thumbnail differ from the artist's official album artwork, even though the title text matches?
questions.say_example: The artwork on this one doesn't match the original release - could be a cover, karaoke, or remix. Still want it, or should I find the original?

questions.question: Is the text of the newly added track solid, or is it visually greyed out?
questions.why: Platforms visually grey out tracks that are region-locked, removed by the label, or otherwise unplayable in your current territory, even though they can still be searched and added to playlists.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to instantly realize the agent added a dead catalog track that will be silently skipped during playback.
questions.check: Does the newly added track's title appear greyed out rather than solid text?
questions.say_example: The newly added track's title is greyed out

children.label: Manage the playlist
children.note: whatever the state calls for: 8.1 to re-edit; 8.2 to organize the sidebar; 8.3 to share; 8.4 for offline copies; 8.5 to keep listening

questions.question: Do you want to modify the playlist's title or description?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Playlist Description' dialog containing the text 'Work Playlist 1', presenting an option to update the playlist's details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent automatically dismisses this dialog, you lose the chance to customize the playlist's description or name for better organization.
questions.verify_form: An edit dialog for the title and description was open - check whether the agent changed it or dismissed it; a dismissal leaves the default name standing.
questions.check: Does a dialog show the current title or description, open for editing?
questions.say_example: Left the title and description as they were

questions.question: How do you want to customize the details and appearance of this new playlist?
questions.why: The new playlist screen currently displays generic cover art and no description, requiring a decision on whether to use the three-dot menu to edit these details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personalize the playlist's visual identity and context with your own preferred artwork and text.
questions.verify_form: The agent chose whether to customize the new playlist - check the cover, name, and description it left behind; the defaults are generic art and no description.
questions.check: Does the new playlist show generic cover art and no description by default?
questions.say_example: Left the default cover and no description on the new playlist

questions.question: Should you use the 'Add Songs' button or open the three-dot menu to manage this empty playlist?
questions.why: The screen shows the newly created playlist is empty and provides an 'Add Songs' button, but other management options are hidden in the menu.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to review or modify the new playlist's settings before adding songs to it.
questions.verify_form: The agent either started adding songs or opened the management menu first - check which happened, and whether the playlist's settings were reviewed before it filled.
questions.check: Does the empty playlist show both an 'Add Songs' button and a separate three-dot menu?
questions.say_example: Went straight to Add Songs rather than the management menu

questions.question: Do you want to adjust any settings or management options for your new playlist?
questions.why: The menu displays options like editing, sharing, or making the playlist public, which control how the playlist is accessed and organized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to discover and configure privacy, sharing, and editing features for your newly created playlist.
questions.verify_form: The management menu listed edit, delete, and make-public - check whether the agent touched any of them; delete sits one row from edit.
questions.check: Does the management menu list edit, delete, and make-public options next to each other?
questions.say_example: Delete sits right next to edit in this menu - staying clear of it

questions.question: Which existing playlists do you want to group into the new folder?
questions.why: The sidebar displays a newly created folder alongside existing playlists, presenting an opportunity to organize the library.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally organize your music library by deciding which specific playlists belong together.
questions.verify_form: The agent grouped playlists into the folder - check which ones moved; the folder plays as one aggregate list, so membership changes what actually plays.
questions.check: Does the sidebar show a newly created folder alongside existing playlists?
questions.say_example: Grouped <the named playlists> into the new folder

questions.question: What do you want to name this new folder?
questions.why: The screen shows a new 'untitled folder' nested inside the 'Workout' folder, which needs a specific name to properly organize the playlists.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose the exact name and organizational hierarchy for your new playlist folders.
questions.verify_form: The agent named the new folder - check the sidebar; an untitled folder buries the playlists it holds.
questions.check: Does the sidebar show an untitled folder nested inside the named parent folder?
questions.say_example: Named the new folder <a descriptive name>

questions.question: Do you want the new folder nested inside the current one or at the root level?
questions.why: The screen showed the new folder automatically nested inside the currently selected folder, which dictates how your library is organized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control the exact visual hierarchy and grouping of your playlist folders.
questions.verify_form: The new folder landed somewhere in the hierarchy - check whether it sits inside the other folder or at the root; the platform quietly nests it inside whatever was selected.
questions.check: Is the new folder shown nested inside the currently selected folder rather than at the root?
questions.say_example: Nested the new folder inside <the parent folder>

questions.question: Do you want to make this playlist public on your profile or share it with anyone?
questions.why: The playlist view includes a checkbox to publish it on your profile and a menu with options to share it via link, email, or messages.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over the privacy of your playlist and the choice of who gets to see or access it.
questions.verify_form: The publish and share controls were on screen - check whether the playlist got published to the profile or a link went out; either makes the list visible beyond you.
questions.check: Does the playlist view show a public-profile toggle, a share menu, or a 'copy link' action that would expose it beyond you?
questions.say_example: This playlist can go public on your profile, or you can share a link to it. Want either, or keep it just yours?

questions.question: Do you want to download the playlist for offline listening?
questions.why: The screen displays a download button next to the play button, offering the option to save the tracks locally.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to use your device's storage to make these songs available without an internet connection.
questions.verify_form: The download toggle was available - check whether the playlist is now marked downloaded; that spends your device's storage and was never part of the add.
questions.check: Does the playlist view show a separate download/offline toggle distinct from any add-to-playlist control?
questions.say_example: That download toggle saves it offline - it doesn't add anything new to the playlist

questions.question: Do you want to remove the downloaded playlist from your device?
questions.why: The playlist view displays a green download icon indicating the songs are currently saved locally, which consumes device storage.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their device's local storage management and offline listening capabilities.
questions.verify_form: The download was removable - check the download icon's state; undownloading frees storage but kills offline listening.
questions.check: Does the playlist show a green download icon indicating it's saved locally?
questions.say_example: Removed the offline download, freeing up storage

questions.question: Which song do you want to select from the playlist?
questions.why: The screen displayed a list of 93 liked songs, requiring a choice of which specific track to interact with.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally browse their saved tracks and spontaneously choose which one to play.
questions.verify_form: The agent played one track off the list - check which one; if you wanted a specific song heard, a different pick is not it.
questions.check: Does the playlist list multiple songs to choose from?
questions.say_example: Selected <a track> from the playlist

questions.question: Do you want to start playing the playlist?
questions.why: The screen shows a prominent green play button on the 'Cool vibes' playlist, allowing immediate playback.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to listen to the playlist immediately after verifying its contents.
questions.verify_form: Starting playback was optional - check whether the agent hit play; an unrequested play takes over whatever you were listening to.
questions.check: Does the playlist view show a prominent play button?
questions.say_example: Started the playlist playing

questions.question: Do you want to shuffle the playback order?
questions.why: The Now Playing view displays playback controls, including a shuffle icon that determines if the songs will play randomly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the ability to decide whether to experience the playlist sequentially or in a randomized order.
questions.verify_form: The shuffle toggle was right there - check its state; shuffled playback ignores the order you just curated.
questions.check: Does the Now Playing view show a shuffle control?
questions.say_example: Left shuffle off, keeping the curated order

questions.question: Is the playlist view back on screen after minimizing the player?
questions.why: The down arrow icon in the top left minimizes the full-screen player so you can see the underlying playlist.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the spatial awareness of how the active player overlays the main navigation and playlist views.
questions.check: Does minimizing the full-screen player reveal the playlist view underneath?
questions.say_example: Minimized the player back to the playlist view

questions.question: Should I add this song to your queue to play next?
questions.why: The context menu for the song in the playlist view offers an 'Add to queue' option.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to line up the newly added song to listen to right away.
questions.verify_form: The agent could queue the new song - check the queue contents; queuing changes what plays next on your device right now.
questions.check: Does the context menu offer 'Add to queue' as an action separate from adding to a named playlist?
questions.say_example: Add to queue only plays it next - it won't end up saved in <the playlist>

questions.question: Is the added song actually saved in the playlist, or only sitting in the play queue?
questions.why: Checking the 'Next In Queue' and 'Next From' sections allows you to verify if the song was successfully added to your upcoming playback.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the opportunity to review your upcoming playback order and visually confirm that the right tracks are queued.
questions.check: Does the newly added song appear in the 'Next in Queue' list while the playlist itself does not list it?
questions.say_example: This song is sitting in the play queue, not saved in the playlist itself

questions.question: Did the skip and back controls change the playing track as expected?
questions.why: The player controls display previous and next arrow buttons next to the play icon, which allow you to navigate through the tracks.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this task means you lose the ability to manually control playback and instantly skip or replay specific songs while listening.
questions.check: Do the skip and back controls change which track is currently playing?
questions.say_example: Skipped ahead to <the next track>

children.label: Bring over an existing collection
children.note: 9.1 through 9.3 in the transfer app, then 9.4 back in the library; an in-service copy uses 2.6, 4, 5.4, and 7 instead
